xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4333: Session Vault: key rotation after device loss (key ring, re-encrypt refs under a new key)

plan.title: Session Vault: key rotation after device loss (key ring, re-encrypt refs under a new key)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: Rotation is one security feature whose parts cannot ship separately without harm: a rotation verb without the key-guarded store would let stale machines keep writing under the retired key (or mint truncated records), and without the tolerant readers every sync after a rotation throws on the retired-ref markers. The surface is 26 files because each production module carries its own named test file; every file sits inside the standalone Session Vault (src/lib/vault, src/cli/commands/vault, their tests) plus two doc pages and one skill.

narratives.Problem: Revoking or losing a device stops it syncing, but it still holds the vault key K in ${OVERDECK_HOME}/vault/key, so anyone holding it can decrypt any vault ciphertext they obtain, including everything written after the loss. The vault key has never been rotatable: record and machine ref names are HMACs under K, VaultStore has only single-ref CAS, readers throw on any ref sealed under another key, and the docs state that the key never changes.
narratives.Proposal: Add pan vault rotate-key. It saves a new key K' to vault/key.next, then in ONE atomic VaultStore.casRefs batch writes every record and machine ref re-sealed under K' at its new name, overwrites every old name with a retired-ref marker sealed under the old key, and swaps the header to K' carrying a key ring of retired keys. Chunks and WIP parts are not rewritten; decodeChunk/decodeWipParts fall back through VaultSubkeys.previous loaded from the header ring. openVault builds a KeyGuardedStore that asserts the verified header version on every ref write and re-checks it after refresh, so a machine holding a retired key is refused with a re-join instruction. The keywrap is re-wrapped or removed, a new recovery phrase is printed, re-join replaces the key in place and discards unpublished objects, sync/status skip refs they cannot open, and the docs describe rotation. Full design, decisions D-1..D-18 and requirements FR-1..FR-13 / NFR-1..NFR-5 are in .pan/drafts/PAN-4333.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Re-encrypting existing chunks, settlement-archive chunks or WIP parts under the new key
- Deleting refs or objects from any backend, or garbage-collecting retired-ref markers and orphan objects
- Adding a ref-delete operation to VaultStore
- Implementing the hosted overdeck:// store, device revocation, pan account, or editing configuration/anywhere-sign-in.mdx (PAN-4297, PAN-4330)
- Automatic rotation (on revoke or on a schedule) or any dashboard UI for rotation
- Rotating the user's git credentials
- Removing keys from the key ring
- Approve-from-another-device key transfer
- Any change to the chunk, WIP-part or keywrap/v1 wire formats

autoDecisions.summary: Store the key ring (retired keys, newest first) inside the encrypted h/header value, not in a local file.
autoDecisions.rationale: Only holders of the current key can read it, and any machine that obtains the current key by phrase or passphrase gets the ring on its next header read with no extra transfer step.

autoDecisions.summary: Re-encrypt refs only; old chunks and WIP parts stay under their original key and are read through VaultSubkeys.previous.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks to keep older chunks readable through a key ring so history need not be re-encrypted in one pass; refs are small and must be re-encrypted because their names derive from K.

autoDecisions.summary: Overwrite each old ref name with a retired-ref marker sealed under the old key instead of deleting it.
autoDecisions.rationale: settle.ts mints a truncated record when an owned record's ref is absent; a non-session value makes it return excluded instead, and VaultStore has no delete.

autoDecisions.summary: Add VaultStore.casRefs (all-or-nothing multi-ref CAS with assert-only ops) and commit the whole rotation in one call.
autoDecisions.rationale: The git backend pushes once per casRef, so a per-ref rotation would expose a long half-rotated window; one batch is one commit, and the same primitive lets every write assert the header version.

autoDecisions.summary: Guard every CLI write with a KeyGuardedStore built in openVault that asserts the verified header version.
autoDecisions.rationale: A stale machine must never publish new data under a retired key; one entry point guards every verb without editing each one.

autoDecisions.summary: Add VaultStore.discardUnpublished and call it before the rotation batch and when a re-join replaces the key.
autoDecisions.rationale: The git backend publishes every untracked object with the next ref write, so objects a stale machine sealed under the retired key would otherwise be pushed after it re-joins.

autoDecisions.summary: Verb name pan vault rotate-key with --yes, --passphrase-file, --generate-passphrase, --no-passphrase; TTY confirmation, --yes required off a TTY.
autoDecisions.rationale: Mirrors pan vault setup's passphrase flags; rotation forces every other machine to re-join, so it deserves an explicit confirmation.

autoDecisions.summary: Rotation is resumable from vault/key.next; the new phrase prints before key.next is removed; batch conflicts retry up to 5 times.
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches setup.ts's rule that the key is saved before the backend changes, and no verb can show a phrase later.

autoDecisions.summary: Do not wait for PAN-4330 or PAN-4297 and do not edit configuration/anywhere-sign-in.mdx (it does not exist).
autoDecisions.rationale: Rotation uses only VaultStore methods, so it works on git and dir now and on a hosted store that passes the shared contract suite; PAN-4330's revocation note can link to the new session-vault section.

autoDecisions.summary: Readers (sync, status) skip refs they cannot open and report retired/unreadable counts.
autoDecisions.rationale: Retired-ref markers are permanently unreadable under the current key, and a junk ref from a revoked device with write access must not break every sync.

narrative.Action: Implement PRD section 7 and work item WI-1. In src/lib/vault/store/types.ts add `export interface RefOp { name: string; expectedVersion: string | null; value?: Uint8Array }` and two VaultStore methods with doc comments: `casRefs(ops: ReadonlyArray<RefOp>): Promise<CasResult>` (all-or-nothing: when every op's ref is at expectedVersion, write every op that carries a value and publish them together; otherwise write nothing and return 'conflict'; throw Error for duplicate names; an op without value only asserts) and `discardUnpublished(): Promise<void>` (drop objects no ref write has published; a backend that publishes on write resolves at once). GitVaultStore: generalize casRefSerialized into a casRefs cycle under the existing casQueue + clone lock: refreshUnlocked, compare remoteBlobSha for every op, return 'conflict' on any mismatch, writeAtomic every valued op, `add -A -- .`, commit with message 'vault: settle' when exactly one valued op else 'vault: batch', push; keep the existing non-fast-forward retry (3) and offline reset/clean rules; make casRef call casRefs([{ name, expectedVersion, value }]). discardUnpublished on git: under the clone lock, `reset --hard origin/main` when origin/main exists, then `git clean -fdq -- objects refs`. DirVaultStore: casRefs inside casQueue nests withFileLock on each op's `<ref>.lock` in ascending name order, compares every refVersion, then writeAtomic every valued op; casRef delegates; discardUnpublished resolves without doing anything. Add contract cases in tests/unit/lib/vault/store/contract.ts: 'casRefs.ac1: writes every valued op when all versions match', 'casRefs.ac2: one stale version writes nothing and returns conflict', 'casRefs.ac3: an assert-only op gates the batch and is never written', 'casRefs.ac4: duplicate names throw', 'discardUnpublished.ac1: an object put but never published is gone after discardUnpublished on git and still present on dir' (branch on the backend name the suite receives; never skipIf). Add to the git suite: 'a batch of three valued ops adds exactly one commit to origin/main'. No execSync, no git stash.

narrative.Action: Implement decision D-7 and WI-3 in a new module src/lib/vault/keyring.ts that imports only Node built-ins and sibling vault modules. Export: `class VaultKeyMismatchError extends Error` (the header is absent or does not open with the key); `class VaultKeyRetiredError extends Error` whose message is `This machine's vault key was retired by a key rotation. Run: pan vault join ${backend} with the new recovery phrase or passphrase.` (backend passed in, default '<backend>'); `async function openKeyring(store: VaultStore, key: Uint8Array, options?: { backend?: string }): Promise<{ keys: VaultSubkeys; store: VaultStore; headerVersion: string; rotatedAt: string | null }>` which readRefs HEADER_REF_NAME, throws VaultKeyMismatchError when absent or when readVaultHeader returns null or throws VaultAuthenticationError, derives subkeys of `key`, sets `keys.previous = parseKeyRing(header).map(deriveSubkeys)`, and returns a KeyGuardedStore; and `class KeyGuardedStore implements VaultStore` wrapping the inner store: casRef(name, expected, value) = casRefs([{ name, expectedVersion: expected, value }]); casRefs(ops) = inner.casRefs([...ops, { name: HEADER_REF_NAME, expectedVersion: headerVersion }]) and on 'conflict' re-read the header: if its version differs and it does not open with the key, throw VaultKeyRetiredError, else return 'conflict'; refresh() = inner.refresh() then re-read the header: same version returns, a different version that still opens with the key adopts the new version and reloads keys.previous in place, otherwise throw VaultKeyRetiredError; putSlot(name, bytes) = this.refresh() then inner.putSlot; putObjects/getObject/hasObjects/readRef/listRefs/discardUnpublished pass through. Tests in tests/unit/lib/vault/keyring.test.ts with a DirVaultStore in a temp dir: 'guard.ac1: a casRef after the header changed under another key throws VaultKeyRetiredError and writes nothing', 'guard.ac2: refresh throws VaultKeyRetiredError once the header no longer opens', 'guard.ac3: putSlot on a retired key throws and leaves keywrap/v1 unchanged', 'guard.ac4: openKeyring loads keyRing entries into keys.previous', 'guard.ac5: casRef on a current header writes normally'.

narrative.Action: Implement PRD section 8 and decisions D-4, D-5, D-9, D-11, D-14 in a new module src/lib/vault/rotate.ts that imports only Node built-ins and sibling vault modules and never imports store/dir.js or store/git.js. Export nextKeyPath() = join(vaultDir(), 'key.next'), loadNextKey(): Promise<Buffer | null> (null on ENOENT, throws on wrong length), saveNextKey(key) (0600, temp file + rename like saveVaultKey), clearNextKey() (unlink, ignore ENOENT), `class VaultRotationConflictError extends Error` with message 'Another machine kept writing to the vault. Stop pan vault on your other machines and run pan vault rotate-key again.', and `rotateVaultKey(options: { store: VaultStore; currentKey: Buffer; keywrap?: Uint8Array | null; now?: () => Date; maxAttempts?: number }): Promise<{ newKey: Buffer; records: number; machines: number; resumed: boolean; committed: 'now' | 'earlier' }>`. Steps: (1) K' = loadNextKey() ?? createVaultKey() then saveNextKey; resumed = key.next already existed. (2) loop up to maxAttempts (default 5): store.refresh(); read h/header; if it opens with K' set committed='earlier' and leave the loop; if it opens with currentKey continue, else throw Error('The vault key on this machine does not open the vault; nothing was rotated.'). (3) store.discardUnpublished(). (4) for every listRefs('r/') and listRefs('m/') entry: readRef, decrypt with keys(currentKey), skip on VaultAuthenticationError, skip values whose type is neither 'session' nor 'machine'; newName = refName('record', value.vaultId, keys(K').K_ref) or refName('machine', value.environmentId, ...); push op { name: newName, expectedVersion: (await store.readRef(newName))?.version ?? null, value: encryptRef(newName, value, keys(K')) } and op { name: oldName, expectedVersion: ref.version, value: encryptRef(oldName, { v:1, type:'retired', at }, keys(currentKey)) }; push header op { name: HEADER_REF_NAME, expectedVersion: header.version, value: encryptRef(HEADER_REF_NAME, { ...oldHeader, rotatedAt: at, keyRing: [currentKey base64, ...(oldHeader.keyRing ?? [])] }, keys(K')) }. (5) casRefs(ops): ok → committed='now', leave the loop; conflict → next attempt; after maxAttempts throw VaultRotationConflictError; VaultOfflineError propagates with key.next kept. (6) keywrap undefined → nothing; Uint8Array → store.putSlot(KEYWRAP_OBJECT_NAME, bytes); null → store.putSlot(KEYWRAP_OBJECT_NAME, null). (7) saveVaultKey(K'). Do NOT clear key.next here; the CLI clears it after printing the phrase. encryptRef needs the RetiredRefMarker union from keyring-format. Tests in tests/unit/lib/vault/rotate.test.ts (temp OVERDECK_HOME, DirVaultStore; settle real transcripts with settle() to create records): 'rotate.ac1: after rotation every record and machine is readable under K' at its new name with identical content', 'rotate.ac2: every old name holds a retired marker sealed under K', 'rotate.ac3: a pre-rotation chunk decodes via the ring loaded by openKeyring', 'rotate.ac4: a crash after the commit (throwing from the keywrap putSlot) resumes with the same K' and committed: earlier', 'rotate.ac5: a conflicting write between read and commit is retried and the final vault includes it' (wrap the store so the first casRefs first performs a concurrent casRef then returns conflict), git: 'rotate.ac6: the rotation adds exactly one commit to the bare remote'. No sleeps in the retry loop.

narrative.Action: Implement decisions D-11, D-12, D-13, D-15 and WI-7. Register in src/cli/commands/vault/index.ts: `vault.command('rotate-key').description('Replace the vault key after losing a device: re-encrypt refs under a new key, keep old chunks readable, print a new recovery phrase').option('--yes', 'Rotate without the confirmation prompt').option('--passphrase-file <path>', 'Re-wrap passphrase unlock under the new key with the passphrase in this file').option('--generate-passphrase', 'Re-wrap passphrase unlock under the new key with a generated 6-word passphrase, printed once').option('--no-passphrase', 'Turn passphrase unlock off').action(lazyAction(() => import('./rotate-key.js'), 'rotateKeyCommand'))`, and change the passphrase group description to 'Turn passphrase unlock for new machines on (set) or off (remove); the vault key stays the same'. New src/cli/commands/vault/rotate-key.ts exporting `rotateKeyCommand(options, io = defaultIo)`: readVaultConfig (no backend → print VAULT_OFF_MESSAGE, return); loadVaultKey (missing → io.err join hint, exit 1); store = storeForBackend(config.backend) (do NOT use openVault: it refuses while key.next exists); refuse --passphrase-file with --generate-passphrase; resumed = (await loadNextKey()) !== null; unless resumed or --yes: off a TTY print 'Pass --yes to rotate the vault key without a prompt.' and exit 1; on a TTY ask 'Rotate the vault key? Every other machine must re-join with the new recovery phrase or passphrase. [y/N] ' and stop (exit 0, print 'Nothing was changed.') unless the answer is y or yes. Keywrap choice, all decided BEFORE rotateVaultKey: hasWrap = (await store.getObject(KEYWRAP_OBJECT_NAME)) !== null; --no-passphrase → keywrap null when hasWrap else undefined; --passphrase-file → read, checkPassphraseStrength (fail → print message, exit 1); --generate-passphrase → generatePassphrase(); no flag and hasWrap and TTY → choosePassphrase(io, {}); no flag and hasWrap and not TTY → print 'This vault has a passphrase. Pass --passphrase-file <path>, --generate-passphrase or --no-passphrase.' and exit 1; no flag and no wrap → keywrap undefined. Every refusal above (flag conflict, confirmation declined, strength failure, missing flag) happens BEFORE key.next exists, so a refused run leaves no pending rotation. Only after the passphrase choice is settled compute K' via loadNextKey() ?? (createVaultKey() then saveNextKey()), wrap with wrapVaultKey(K', passphrase) when a passphrase was chosen, and pass the bytes to rotateVaultKey, which reuses the same key.next. Call rotateVaultKey; on VaultOfflineError print `Backend ${backend} is unreachable; nothing was rotated. Run pan vault rotate-key again.` and exit 1; on VaultRotationConflictError print its message and exit 1. On success print in order: `Vault key rotated for ${backend}: ${records} conversation(s) and ${machines} machine(s) re-encrypted.`, '', 'Write down your NEW recovery phrase. It is shown only now:', '', `  ${keyToPhrase(newKey)}`, '', `The old recovery phrase no longer opens this vault. On every other machine run: pan vault join ${backend}`, then 'Passphrase unlock now uses the new key.' (plus GENERATED_PASSPHRASE_PREFIX + passphrase when generated) or 'Passphrase unlock is off.' or PASSPHRASE_LATER_HINT; then clearNextKey(). Update sync-sources/skills/pan-vault/SKILL.md: add a '## Key rotation (lost device)' section with the four flag lines and one paragraph on what rotation protects and that other machines re-join; replace 'and the vault key never changes' with 'and setting or removing a passphrase does not change the vault key'. Tests in tests/unit/cli/vault/rotate-key.test.ts (dir backend fixture): 'cli.ac1: --yes --no-passphrase rotates, prints 24 words that decode to the new key file, and deletes keywrap/v1', 'cli.ac2: non-TTY without --yes exits 1 and the backend refs are unchanged', 'cli.ac3: a vault with a keywrap and no passphrase flag off a TTY exits 1 before any write', 'cli.ac4: --generate-passphrase publishes a keywrap that unwraps to the new key with the printed passphrase', 'cli.ac5: key.next is gone after a successful run'.

narrative.Action: Implement decision D-10, FR-12 and WI-8 in src/cli/commands/vault/join.ts. (1) When an existing git clone is opened (not createdClone) refresh it before reading anything on every path, not only the passphrase path; VaultOfflineError keeps the local view as today.
